project.name: dream-net
project.summary: DreamWeave's networking substrate: secure UDP between authenticated peers, with reliable-ordered and unreliable event channels and a schema handshake.
project.license: (MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND BSD-3-Clause AND ISC

credits.name: Más Bandwidth LLC
credits.role: netcode, reliable and serialize, the crates dream-net is built on

notes.summary: Fixes AEAD nonce reuse in the netcode handshake (GHSA-8mrq-q9c6-h23v) by moving to netcode 1.5.0 and the NETCODE 1.03 protocol. 2.1.0 peers do not connect to 2.0.0 or 1.x peers: upgrade servers and clients together.
changed: The vendored C netcode is v1.5.0 (from v1.4.10), with the same three local patches. Every connection attempt draws a fresh client salt, every server mapping a fresh nonce, and the packet keys are derived from them and the token's keys, so no two attempts or servers ever share a key.

A client no longer refuses a token it already passed to `connect` in the same process. That was 2.0.0's stopgap for this advisory; netcode now makes a token used twice safe, and the server enforces one attempt per token, holding an unfinished token only for the address and salt that first presented it, for the token's timeout. Still mint a new token for every attempt.
fixed: GHSA-8mrq-q9c6-h23v: with netcode 1.4.10 and earlier, a retried unfinished handshake with the same connect token, or one token listing several servers, could encrypt different packets under the same key and nonce, which exposes plaintext and allows forging those packets. 2.0.0 blocked the retried handshake within one process only; 1.x did not block it at all.
breaking: The netcode protocol is NETCODE 1.03, where 2.0.0 and every 1.x release speak NETCODE 1.02. Peers of the two never connect: a server ignores the other protocol's connection requests, so the client's attempt ends with `ConnectFailed { reason: TimedOut }`. dream-net's own wire format is unchanged.

notes.summary: The transport now runs on Más Bandwidth's C netcode and reliable, vendored and compiled in, with single-use connect tokens and restart protection. The wire format is unchanged, so 2.0.0 and 1.x peers still connect to each other.
added: `Server::with_max_token_lifetime` and `DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECT_TOKEN_LIFETIME`, to set the token lifetime the start floor is built on.
changed: netcode-official, reliable and serialize-official are gone from the dependency graph. The vendored C (netcode v1.4.10 with three local patches, reliable v1.4.6, and netcode's libsodium subset) is pinned file by file and checked against upstream. The wire format is written by dream-net's own safe Rust and is byte-for-byte unchanged.
The license expression is `(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND BSD-3-Clause AND ISC`: dream-net's own code is unchanged, and the vendored C carries its own terms. `NOTICE.md` reproduces every notice.
`MemoryUsage::reliable` is now an upper bound on reliable's endpoint, about 581 KB with the default `TransportConfig`, almost all of it fragment reassembly an idle connection does not hold.

A server holds its port exclusively on every platform: it fails to start when any other socket holds the port, and nothing can bind the port on one of its addresses afterwards. Windows allowed both before.

A client that finds a schema or protocol mismatch reports `ConnectFailed` at once, but keeps its session for `mismatch_linger` seconds, sending only its hello, so the server can report the mismatch too.
fixed: A server could report nothing for a client with a mismatched schema, when the client's hello and its disconnect arrived in the same update. 1.1.1 has the same gap.
On Windows a server could start on a port another program held on one address, and lose the traffic for that address to it without an error.
On Windows the cause of a socket failure, such as a port in use, was lost before it reached `Error::Netcode`.
breaking: Building needs Clang 18 or newer (Apple Clang 16 on macOS): `build.rs` compiles the vendored C and refuses GCC, MSVC's `cl` and fast-math flags rather than fall back. The crate declares `links = "dream_net_native"`.

`Error::Netcode` and `generate_connect_token` now carry `NetcodeError`, dream-net's own type with the same variants and texts as netcode-official's `Error` plus `InvalidConnectTokenLifetime`. Code that named or matched the old type must use `NetcodeError`.

`TransportConfig::reliable_config` returns `ReliableConfig` and `Connection::reliable_counters` returns `&ReliableCounters`, dream-net's own types, in place of the reliable crate's `Config` and `Counters`.
`TransportConfig::validate` refuses `sent_packets_buffer_size` and `received_packets_buffer_size` above 16384, the C reliable's limit; 1.1.1 allowed 32768.

Connect tokens are single use: a client refuses a token already passed to `connect` in the same process, and a server refuses one that already established a session there, even after that session ended.

A server refuses tokens that expire within its maximum token lifetime (30 seconds by default) of its start, so a token minted before a restart cannot open a second session; a 30-second token minted in the server's start second is refused too.

notes.summary: Requires a ctutils with RUSTSEC-2026-0385 fixed, for the constant-time comparison behind netcode's packet authentication.
fixed: ctutils before 0.4.4 could generate branches on secret values in its constant-time masks and comparisons (RUSTSEC-2026-0385). netcode's Poly1305 tag verification goes through it, so dream-net now requires ctutils 0.4.4 or newer, which also moves projects whose lockfiles still held an older version.

notes.summary: A peer is announced before its first event, captures without payloads keep their lengths, and the codec's decode errors are standard Rust errors.
added: `wire::DecodeError` and `wire::Malformed` implement `std::error::Error`, and `DecodeError` implements `Display`, like the crate's other errors: a malformed packet prints its reason, which is also its `source()`, and a mismatch prints the foreign hello.
fixed: `Server` and `Client` queued `Connected` after the events of the packet that completed the handshake, so a host could poll a peer's `Message` before its `Connected`. `Connected` now comes first.
`CaptureWriter` without payloads wrote each event's length from its payload, so a capture read back and written again recorded every event as zero bytes. It now writes the record's `len`.

notes.summary: First release: secure UDP between authenticated peers, reliable-ordered and unreliable event channels, and a schema handshake, over the Más Bandwidth netcode, reliable and serialize crates.
added: A frozen `Schema` of channels and events: event ids from sorted names, never registration order, and a 128-bit fingerprint (truncated SHA-256) peers compare before any event is accepted.
Reliable-ordered channels, delivered exactly once in send order and resent until acknowledged, and unreliable-unordered channels with a choice of overflow policy.
Many events aggregated into each packet, and events larger than a datagram fragmented by reliable.

`Server` and `Client` over netcode: connect tokens, encryption, generation-checked `PeerId` handles, and polled lifecycle events, including schema and protocol mismatches reported with both fingerprints on both ends.
Bounded memory on every queue: pending, parked and pooled bytes, with at most `max_pending_bytes + 2 * max_parked_bytes` held per connection on receive.
Protocol captures at the host boundary, in a versioned binary format that carries the schema's names.
`Connection` independent of sockets, and a deterministic link simulator for tests and benchmarks.
Wire format 2, pinned by golden bytes; warm send and receive paths that allocate nothing; fuzz harnesses, a soak test and Criterion benchmarks.
